claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children are you looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my child Alex, who's 14 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I have a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care?** For example, does Alex live with you, or do you pay towards their upbringing (such as for food, clothing, or accommodation)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives with me and I look after them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that.

**Are you and Alex living in the United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, or Northern Ireland)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, we don't live in the UK. We live abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you live abroad, I need to ask a couple of follow-up questions to determine if you might still be eligible.

**Are you or your partner (if you have one) currently working and paying National Insurance contributions in the UK, or receiving certain UK benefits like a State Pension or contribution-based Jobseeker's Allowance?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not working in the UK or paying National Insurance there, and I'm not receiving any UK benefits either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

One more question: **Are you a Crown servant (for example, a diplomat or member of the armed forces) posted overseas, or are you the family member of a Crown servant posted overseas?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant and I'm not a family member of one either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for providing all of this information. Based on what you've told me, I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

**For Alex (age 14):** To claim Child Benefit, you generally need to be living in the United Kingdom. While there are some exceptions for people living abroad—such as being a Crown servant posted overseas, working in the UK and paying National Insurance, or receiving certain UK benefits—you've confirmed that none of these circumstances apply to you.

Since you and Alex live abroad and you don't meet any of the qualifying exceptions, you unfortunately cannot claim Child Benefit at this time.

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you move back to the UK—you may become eligible, and I'd encourage you to look into claiming then.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

There are some exceptions that allow people living abroad to claim, such as: (1) being a Crown servant posted overseas (e.g., diplomat or armed forces member), or (2) working in the UK and paying National Insurance contributions, or (3) receiving certain UK benefits. The claimant has confirmed they live abroad with Alex, are not working in the UK or paying National Insurance, are not receiving UK benefits, and are not a Crown servant or family member of one. Therefore, they do not meet the residency requirements or any of the exceptions for claiming Child Benefit for Alex.
